You ask her why she is here and not up in the North Pole at this time of year. She reaches forward to grab your hands and bring them up to her tits as she replies. You grope them happily, the massive mounds over flowing from your hands.

<>I’m here to help silly! You need help getting gifts for all of those lovely ladies in your life. Only one person can give gifts better than I can. And he’s a bit preoccupied at the moment<>

You continue to grope, your hands almost completely sinking into her soft tits. You thank her for coming to help you. But, you’re struggling to know how she can help when you can hardly imagine anything good to get all of your loved ones.

<>Oh that’s the easy part. Just one flick and just like how your perverted little mind got my tits out, their minds will create the gifts that they want more than anything else. They are gonna cost money though. That’s the secret of Christmas magic that Nick doesn’t like me telling people. Money is the source of it all. People buy gifts is what give him all his power! Like the power to be my sugar daddy for instance. Now I’ll be here in the mall. Come to me when you have some cash to buy the gifts. Bring them to the right person and you’ll be rewarded no doubt! And if you spread enough Christmas cheer, I’ll spread some more to you to top it all off<>

She winks at you cutely as she finishes explaining what you need to do. But you still have a question on your mind. Why do you have to guess which gift will go to which girl? Why can’t she just tell you?

<>Because I’m here to help silly, not just give you all the answers! Kids today I swear you want everything handed to you. Don’t worry, it shouldn’t be tough at all as long as you listen to them while they talk. Women tend to leave hint where you least expect them! Visit me soon, naughty boy<>

With another swish of her hand she disappears, leaving you with your hands reach out in front of you and a bulge forming in your pants. A few people pass by giving you odd looks at the pose you are in. You just stand up and walk away, heading back to meet up with your Mother and <>. When you catch up you notice that they each have many bags in each hand.

<>There you are <>$mom.title<>$mc.name<>! We’ve been looking for you. No luck finding anything good huh? Don’t worry, you’ll find something. Sometimes it just isn’t the right day to shop. Like how those shoes I told $sis.name about were gone today, it was a total bummer<> <>Yeah and they were out of my shade of eyeliner too. People really clean the shelves this time of year<>

You agree with them and let them each know that you’re gonna get them something great. They give you a warm smile in return, clearly reassured by your words. Once you three are all finished shopping you head home. You offer to help them carry their bags in, but they refuse, clearly wanting to keep their gifts for you a secret. With nothing to bring in, you stand in the hall of your home, wondering what to do next.

passages.source_raw:
<>

Rich and warm wood smells contrast the harsh smells of metals and chemicals. The confusing and conflicting scents fill your nose the moment you push open the doors to the warehouse. But they aren’t enough to distract you from the booming voice that calls out the second you enter.

<>Come here now, boy!<> [img["ressources/scene/christmas/intro3.webp"]]

That’s Santa, and it’s unmistakable with his hat, beard, and gut. He’s staring you down, standing among the elves that are tirelessly working to continue construction of the gifts for Christmas. The man, known for being jolly, seems to have quite the bone to pick with you. Given how the last two years went for you with Bea and Eris, there’s a clear inkling as to why that might me.

<>You took my wife. And last I checked, you’ve done it twice! You’ve been so naughty, consumed by vice. So tell me why, my list has you nice?<>

Before you can explain or answer him, he cuts you off and continues to speak.

<>It matters not, your place on the list. I have brought you here, to help me with this. I won’t bore you with details, I’ll give you the gist. Magic has laws, and this Santa needs a Miss.<>

Santa needs a wife. It feels logical. As logical as being in the North Pole and speaking to Santa in person can feel that is. He needs a Mrs. Claus. And you are the reason that he currently doesn’t has one. It’s only fair that you help give him a proper replacement at this point. So you ask him what you need to do to help.

<>Here in the North Pole, I have Elves three. Women of beauty, who remain loyal to me. The choice of whom, I leave to thee. Until I am wed, you shall not be free.<>

Three elves, and you have to choose who becomes Santa’s new wife. Seems odd that he would need you to pick. So you ask him why you instead of just doing it himself.

<>You excel at spreading cheer for this holiday season. The women will help you, instruments of your treason. Buy a gift at the market, where your harlots will sleaze in. That will be needed, that is the reason.<>

Santa shoos you away, getting you out of the workshop and back into the snowy cold. Down the candy cane road you see the Market at the center of the village. That is where Santa told you to go. It’s best to just listen, as it doesn’t seem like you’ll be getting out of here until you figure this out for him.

You hear your name called and turn to the source. Rhea is standing at her office door and waves you over. You furrow you brow, wondering what she could possibly want to talk with you about. She herds you into her office and closes the door behind you. Giving you both some privacy. You waste no time in asking her what she wants to discuss. And you make sure to use your tone to indicate that you aren’t happy about being pulled in like this out of the blue.

<>Don’t be so sour. I wanted to give you a compliment<>

You scoff, doubting that someone with the drive and intensity she has would genuinely want to compliment her competition.

<>I’m serious. You’ve impressed me so far. You’re handling a lot of stuff. And with an absolutely lesser Campaign Manager, the fact that you’re in this race is a testament to you<>

You thank her for saying so. Doing so out of politeness, as you still don’t believe she is being genuine. Especially with that back handed remark about your Campaign Manager.

<>I was actually impressed by a little bit more than just how well you’re doing<>

Rhea suddenly leans in close to you. She traces the muscles under your shirt with her finger. Getting her face close to yours as she speaks. You don’t know why, but you can tell right away that she is trying to seduce you.

<>I wonder what else you’re good at<>

She keeps teasing you. She is making it very clear that she wants to fool around with you. Something seems off though. Rhea is a woman of action. So you’re sure that if she implies something then she will likely follow through with it. But you can’t help but feel like fraternizing with your enemy could possibly be a good thing. You could let her continue, but if you want to stop her the time to do so would be now.

[[Let her continue and see where it leads|Rhea Alt Stage 1][$choice to "continue"; $scene to 0]] [[Keep your cool and stop her before anything happens|Rhea Alt Stage 1][$choice to "stop"]] <>

The city hall is a massive building. It is the center of the City’s government, and as such is constantly filled with people. Politicians, staffers, police officers, and disgruntled citizens, all flood the halls of the bustling building. You figure that if you plan on running this building soon, you should familiarize yourself with it as soon as you can. You get past security and head over to the directory. The black board has white letters clipped to it, detailing who is in almost every office, and on which floor they are on.

The Mayor’s office is the first one listed, with the name Cynthia Wallace right beside it. You envision your own name on there one day. But that vision gets cut short as you feel someone suddenly bump into you as they round the corner. You’re not phased much, you merely get pushed a couple inches to the side. But as you turn to see who bumped into you, you notice a small young lady kneeling down to pick up several papers and folders from the floor. You kneel down to help her out, and here her muttering in frustration.

<>Shit...shit...shit, I gotta hurryyyy. She is gonna be pissed if I’m late<>

You grab a few folders and hand them to the woman as she stands up with the rest. She takes them from you smiling brightly.

<>Thank you so much! I’m sorry I ran into you. I’m in a bit of a hurry though! Excuse me!<> [img["ressources/scene/mary/intro.webp"]]

Before she leaves you get a good look at her. She is a very cute young lady. You’re almost disappointed that you don’t get the chance to speak with her more. But just then, you notice a folder on the ground. She forgot one of them. You pick it up and quickly turn to call out to her, but she is already gone. You start walking the halls, heading in the direction she went, and looking for any sign of her. That is when you come across a room with a lot of loud screaming coming out of it.

Considering the distress she sounded like she was in, and the fact that you have one of her folders, you can only assume the screaming is at the young lady who bumped into you. You peak in and realize that you’re looking into the Mayor’s office when you see Cynthia Wallace berating the poor girl.

<>Can you do anything right? I ask you to do one thing, copy some papers and bring them to me. And you manage to fuck that up. Get out of here and get me the rest of my papers before I revoke your internship!<>

The young lady rushes out of Cynthia’s office, turning and bumping into you once again. You joke and say that the two of you have to stop running into each other like this. She looks embarrassed for a moment but as you hand her folder she looks ecstatic.

<>Where did you find this? Oh my lanta you are a live savor thank you so much!<>

You explain that she dropped it and that you’ve been looking for her to give it back. You apologize, noting that you were too late to give it to her before she got yelled at.

<>Oh that? No, no don’t worry. Mayor Wallace can be a bit testy sometimes. But she is a very busy woman. I strive to be as accomplished as she is one day. But I won’t get there messing stuff up as simple as making copies<>

You note that she didn’t mess up, just ran into a speed bump that threw you off a bit.

<>That is so kind of you to say! But it’s still my fault. I ran into you. I didn’t make sure I had everything before I left. I was worried about speed more than accuracy. I should know better. And I will going forward! Oh! I’m Mary by the way, Mary Willis<>

You introduce yourself as well, shaking her hand. He smile beams at you as you great her formally.

<>It has been a pleasure to meet you $mc.name $mc.surname! I hope I’ll see you again soon. But right now I need to get back to work. See ya later!<>

She runs back into Cynthia’s office with the missing folder. You hear more harsh words from Cynthia as you walk away. But after talking with Mary, you’re sure that she can handle it. She seems to like the tough love approach. Although Cynthia seems to like to side more with tough than with love. You consider that something to think about as you work your way towards becoming the Mayor. Putting that to the back of your mind you head back towards the halls. You’ve seen just about all you need to be familiar with the layout of the building. And soon, you’ll be walking through these halls with the familiarity of someone who lives here.

[img["ressources/scene/lee/leeintro.webp"]] <>Good morning and welcome to Chemistry 101. I will be your instructor. My name is Carrie Lee. You all may call me Ms. Lee. If there are no questions, I’d like to get started immediately<>

Her commanding voice has made the class give her their undivided attention. The room falls silent as she listens for a moment. When no one speaks up she turns around and pulls out a marker.

You smile and introduce yourself to her. She hands you one of her pens. Your fingers touch as she hands it too you. She pulls her hand away quickly, an obvious blush forming on her face. You thank her for her help.

You both nod to Ms. Lee, letting her know you both understand.

<>You aren’t wrong, but with our endorsement, Cynthia very well could make up that difference. In fact it was about the difference that she had to overcome in the last election. And after she swept the endorsements she won the vote handily. Are you so sure that working with you is the right choice?<>

You argue that with her endorsement you would be almost assured victory. While telling Bernice that throwing herself in with Cynthia now only gives her the chance to win. And considering some of the bad publicity that Cynthia has gotten over the course of this campaign, it simply makes the most sense to endorse you.

<>I won’t disagree with your admittedly compelling arguments. But, Cynthia is my sister. Where she succeeds I succeed. What do I gain from you winning other than a Mayor who I am on good terms with? I already have that with my own sister, and the family aspect atop it<> <>
[[Offer her the position of Lieutenant Mayor|Bernice Stage 3][$scene to 0; $bernice.choices.stage3 to "offer lt role"]]
<> [[Offer a promise of future roles as you ascend the political ladder|Bernice Stage 3][$scene to 0; $bernice.choices.stage3 to "offer future role"]] [[Warn her of the greater risks she faces by going against you|Bernice Stage 3][$scene to 0; $bernice.choices.stage3 to "warn about risks"]] <>

The City Council is a place where the people of a city can interact with their elected officials directly. So you figure there is no better place to both make your concerns about Mayor Wallace known than in a public forum like this. Especially when you want politically active people to be the ones listening as you call Cynthia out on the bad things she has done. You head into the room and take a seat near the back. Watching to see how the people react to the council in general.

After they go through the usual procedure of bringing up old business from a previous meeting, they open the floor to new business, allowing people to come up to the microphone and publicly petition the Council. You don’t go up right away. You don’t want to try and upstage or overshadow anyone else who might have a more pressing concern. You wait until a few others take a turn of their own before heading up to the podium and giving a speech of your own. You look at the five members of the council, and notice one that stands out among the rest. A rather buxom woman who happens to have the same last name as the Mayor, ‘Wallace’. She looks at you, putting on a polite smile as she watches and waits for you to begin.

[img["ressources/scene/bernice/stage1/intro.webp"]]

A part of you worries that you might have chosen the wrong venue, and that Cynthia’s corruption goes deeper than you might ever know. But, you continue regardless. It would be infinitely more damaging to your campaign if you were to back down now in the face of adversity. You speak loudly and clearly into the podium, making your stand heard. You speak on the Mayor, referring to her as a power hungry and corrupt public official. Such a bold declaration and attack on the Mayor seems to annoy some of the Council members. But with each word you say, the crowd behind you seems to become more and more in your favor.

You rally them up even more, arguing that Cynthia Wallace should step down from her position. Your microphone gets cut off before you can finish your speech. The Council cutting you as you went over the two minutes that they allot every speaker. But you make sure to end your speech loudly enough for all to hear regardless of the microphone. As you head back to your seat, you get several high fives and handshakes from people in the crowd. Making sure to tell all of them that if they want change, they should vote for you this election cycle. And more than a few of them promise that they will.

[[Your speech got someone’s attention|Bernice Stage 1]] <>

Bernice is bent over on the floor of her office, looking for something on the ground. With her ass jutting up in the air, it’s feels like an open invitation for you. You yank her skirt right off and plunge your cock deep into her pussy. She recoils at first, but when she turns back to look at you, she calms down a little. Only a little, though. Enough to let you finish, but not enough to prevent angry rambling after you’re finished.

You don’t stick around to bother listening to her griping afterwords though. You got what you came here for.

<><> <>

You step into Bernice’s office to have a short conversation with the Councilwoman. Its always good to have a strong relationship with the more prominent members of your City Council. You see her sitting behind her desk enjoying what is likely her third cup of coffee of the day. When she sees you enter she pulls the coffee away from her lips, smiling brightly to greet you.

[img["ressources/scene/bernice/locs/council.webp"]] <>Oh hello Mr. $mc.surname, how can I help you today?<>

You ask her if she has a moment to discuss policy with you. She gestures to the seat in front of her as she replies.

<>I’m always happy to speak with my constituents. What is on your mind?<>

You spend the better part of an hour discussing ideas for some of the city’s biggest problems, and leave feeling rather accomplished.

<><> <>

There is nothing to do here right now.

<> [[Leave|City hall]]

passages.name: Court Case Finale
passages.source_raw:
<>

Attention: Once you begin this event, you will not be able to gather further intelligence or strengthen your case any further. You need 100 Case strength in the end, in order to get a conviction in this case. If you fail this, your Uncle will be let go and you will fail. This event cannot be retried later. During the case you may raise the Case strength, but if you are not sure that you will reach 100 case strength, then we recommend you go back and return when you have more.

''Current case strength: $law.police.str'' [[Continue|Court Case Finale][$scene to 1]] [[Go back|Police station]]<> <>

It all happened so fast. Faster than you imagined it would be able to go. You and Liz spoke and agreed that the amount of evidence you’ve gathered at this point, is the most you’ll be able to obtain. It is time to bring the case before a Jury and take your Uncle Roger down. Once and for all. The arrest warrant gets signed, and within an hour the Casino is raided. Several arrests are made, your Uncle chief among them. The holding cells of the precinct gets filled nearly to the brim. You avoid the cells to make sure your Uncle does not see you and figure out that you have been working against him.

He is quickly arraigned, and thankfully he is denied bail do to the severity of his crimes and his flight risk factor. He is taken to county prison to sit and await his trial. A day that arrives very soon after his arrest. Making every conceivable effort to deliver a speedy trial in order to prevent him or his defense from tampering with the jury or any witnesses that might be called. The morning of the trial, the judge enters the courts, and begins the proceedings.

[img["ressources/scene/law/court/judge.webp"]] [[Liz delivers the Prosecution’s opening statement|Court Case Finale][$scene to 2]]<> <>

Liz stands up before the court, looking at the jury, and giving your Uncle a scornful side eye as she passes by him. She smiles and begins speaking with an almost musical tone. Trying to win favor with the jury immediately.

[img["ressources/scene/law/court/liz.webp"]] <>Ladies and Gentlemen of the jury. I stand before you today a proud woman. The brave officers and investigators and officers that I work with, have aided me in building a case full of evidence that I am certain will show you, beyond a reasonable doubt, that the defendant Roger Condamne is a crime lord. A man guilty of so many crimes that it would consume all of our time here today to list them all to you. But to summarize, I will show you evidence that Roger Condamne has been involved in Racketeering, Human Trafficking, Possession and sale of narcotics, and even conspired to commit Murder in the First Degree. While it is my belief that Mr. Condamne’s defense will try and deflect away from these charges. Claim that these acts were committed by people he employs and that he himself had no involvement in them, I can assure you and my opposing council, that we have evidence proving his full knowledge and intent in these crimes as well. I thank you for doing your civic duty today, by presiding over this case. And I look forward to revealing the truth to you all<> [[The defense gives their opening statement|Court Case Finale][$scene to 3]]<> <>

The moment Liz sits back down the attorney defending Uncle Roger stands up and heads to the center of the courtroom, ready to speak in favor of your Uncle to the jury.

<>Ladies and Gentlemen of the jury, my client Mr. Condamne is a simple business man. These charges levied against him are nothing short of slanderous. I will show you, here in this courtroom today, that not only was Mr. Condamne not responsible or involved in these criminal activities that are being alleged today. But in fact, we have every intention of making you all aware of just who is the true culprit. We will show you, that not only is it reasonable to doubt that Mr. Condamne is guilty, but that the true orchestrator, a Mr. $mc.name $mc.surname, is far more likely to be the true mastermind behind these evil, evil deeds. This, combined with evidence of Mr. Condamne’s absence from the country during the time of several of these alleged crimes, will show you that it is purely unreasonable to render a guilty verdict. Thank you all for your time, and I look forward to this being a speedy trial<>

The defense attorney sits back down beside your Uncle Roger. Roger, looking back at you over his chair, and giving you a smug and cross look.

[img["ressources/scene/law/court/uncle.webp"]] [[First arguments|Court Case Finale][$scene to 4]]<> <>

Liz stands before the Judge and jury once more, ready to show the first pieces of evidence against your Uncle. She begins by detailing circumstantial monetary evidence collected against your Uncle. Namely the cost of his large expensive home, and showing that his tax records show a general cost that appears to be substantially greater that the reported income the casino provides. Which leads to Liz begging the obvious question.

<>Just where does this money come from? How is Mr. Condamne paying to keep his Casino afloat despite nearly a decade of losses. And how with such apparent debt racking up can he afford to live so lavishly. If he has a legal explanation, I would love to hear it, and hear why it isn’t noted in any tax record filed in the past thirty years<> [[The defense retorts|Court Case Finale][$scene to 5]]<> <>

Your Uncle Roger’s attorney stands up and goes before the court to present his own arguments. He starts off with a dismissal of Liz’s allusions to the potential illicit sources of Roger’s funds. But then pivots quickly into doing all he can to shift the culpability from your Uncle, onto you.

<>My client does indeed hold a fair bit of debt. But what My opposing council Ms. Bancroft clearly never attempted to look into, is how my client afforded the Casino to begin with. When they became adults, Mr. Condamne inherited a veritable fortune from his father. Who had passed when he was young. He has plenty of money saved in his accounts that are off shore, and do not appear on any physical records in this nation. However, since Ms. Bancroft is so interested in financials, I’m curious if she has looked into my client’s own former nephew. A boy, just barely out of college, appears to be making significant amounts of money on a regular basis. His mother and sister live in a lavishly expensive house, and his mother earns only a professor’s salary. A salary from the very college that Mr. $mc.surname attended. Now far be it from me to accuse Mr. $mc.surname of anything illicit. But, if Mr. Condamne’s financial records are even remotely suspect, I’d say that by comparison Mr. $mc.surname’s finances are down right fraudulent<> [[The first witness, Uncle Roger Himself|Court Case Finale][$scene to 6]]<> <> <>Is the prosecution ready to call it’s first witness?<> <>We are your honor. We are calling Roger Condamne to the stand first<>

The crowd murmurs, shocked to hear that your Uncle is called to the stand so early. The old man slowly stands. His stony expression and icy disposition bleed through with every step. He walks up to the stand, is sworn in to tell the truth, and takes a seat, adjusting himself to get comfortable as he waits for Liz to begin the line of questioning. She starts off, by showing Condamne and the jury pictures of crates filled with illegal items.

<>Mr. Condamne, we have photographic evidence of illegal substances entering and exiting your Casino in massive quantities. Everything from drugs, to firearms, to exotic animals, has gone through the back doors of this building. Now, any responsible business owner would be privy too, if not fully aware of every item brought into his establishment. Especially items in these quantities<> <>Objection your honor. Is there an actual question here?<> <>Sustained. Ms. Bancroft, please expedite this<> <>Of course your honor. Mr. Condamne, did you know about these items being moved in and out of your property?<> <>Absolutely not<> <>Are you then admitting to this court that you are an absentee proprietor?<> <>I am not<> <>Then what are you saying Mr. Condamne? Because to say that you are attentive, yet blissfully unaware of these activities simply does not track logically<> <>I am not saying anything more than the truth. You asked if I know about those items. I did not. You asked if I’m an absentee proprietor. I am not<> <>Then please tell us, how it is that you, as an attentive proprietor, were not aware of all of this illegal activity occurring at your establishment?<> <>I have many employees. One being my own nephew, <>. I cannot say for certain, but I believe that there was a concerted effort to keep me in the dark about these activities<> <>Do you have any proof, or even a shred of evidence to suggest this is the case?<> <>I can only speak to my nephew’s character. And based on what I have learned since he began working for me, I can simply say that his character is lacking<> <>The court is not here today to discuss your nephew, Mr. Condamne. We are all here about you and your activities<> <>My nephew’s activities show that he is much more likely to be at fault for these alleged crimes than I. How can that not be of importance?<> <>Objection, argumentative<> <>Sustained, Mr. Condamne please limit your responses to answering the questions<> <>Apologies your honor, I thought I was just telling the whole truth<> <>Then please what truth is that? What character concerns about your nephew leads you to believe these things about him?<> <>The boy is depraved, and incestuous. He is currently in a sexual relationship, with his mother, sister, his aunt, and his cousin. The latter two happen to be my ex-wife and daughter<> <>Those are bold and possibly slanderous claims Mr. Condamne. Do you have any proof to substantiate these claims?<> <>I do not. But my attorney has plenty of photographic proof<> <>If it would please the court, I’d be happy to submit these photographs into evidence<> <>Objection your honor these photographs were not part of discovery<> <>Overruled. I want to see this evidence. Do you have any further questions, Ms. Bancroft?<> <>Not at this time, your honor<>

Condamne’s attorney passes Liz to bring the photos up to the Judge.

<>Then you may begin your cross examination<> <>We have no questions for Mr. Condamne at this time, your honor<> <>Very well, prosecution may call their next witness<> [[Suzy Marks is called to the stand|Court Case Finale][$scene to 7]]<> <> <>We would like to call to the stand, Officer Suzanne Marks<>

Suzy Marks, the girl that brought you in to speak with your Uncle in the first place, walks up to the stand and is quickly sworn in. The badge on her blazer shows that she must have been working as an informant for Liz in your Uncle’s organization for some time as well. Her taking the stand like this is shockingly brave. She is putting her life on the line.

<>Officer Marks, please tell me what your duties have been for the past several months. And spare no detail from your recount<> <>Well, I’ve been like, undercover for a while. Roger had me working as a fence. Which, did you know you could do that? I thought fences were just those wood walls around houses. I was soooo confused when he asked me to work as one. Anyway, I’ve been selling and buying illegal stuff for him. Mostly drugs. A LOT of drugs<> <>And Officer Marks, where did you get these drugs from?<> <>Someone would just bring them to me. I had this cute storeroom in the back of the Casino. Some hot guy would put stuff back there and then I’d sell it. Roger would even let me set the price because I could just show my tits and make most guys pay whatever I asked them to<> <>And what would you do with the earnings from these illicit sales?<> <>Oh I would hand everything to Roger at the end of the day and he’d pay me based on how much I brought in. I would make bank on topless Tuesdays let me tell ya<> <>And so, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, we have sworn testimony from an Officer of the Law, stating that Mr. Condamne employed this woman to sell illicit items. And then he received almost all of the profit. To further prove this, we would like to display, exhibit C to the court<>

Liz walks over and picks up three evidence bags filled to the brim with bills. She shows them to the jury, flaunting just how heavy they are.

<>This three bags contain all of the money Officer Marks was given during her time undercover within Condamne’s organization. A sum greater than two hundred thousand dollars. All of which has been tested, and does in face contain both the fingerprints of and the DNA of Mr. Condamne. Thank you Officer, no further questions<> [[The defense cross examines|Court Case Finale][$scene to 8]]<> <> <>Officer Marks, forgive me but your explanation of events seems to leave several questions open for me. You say ‘someone’ brought you those illegal items to sell. Was that someone, ever, at ANY point, Mr. Condamne himself?<> <>Uhm, no I don’t think he ever did do it himself, no<> <>So then how could you possibly say that Mr. Condamne had any prior knowledge to what was being sold at this shop?<> <>It was like, in his own casino. He’s a smart man who likes to be nit picky. He knows what is happening in there<> <>Are you in his mind? Because if you can’t read them I don’t see how you could possibly know whether or not he knows something<> <>Well duh, I don’t know. I’m just making like an uh educated guess or whatever<> <>And his lack of presence in this business activity is some how what educated you. No Officer I think that my educated guess is that you misunderstood Mr. Condamne’s instructions, were used by bad actors within the organization, and are now entrapping my client in activities that he had no part to play in, beyond paying his hard working employees a sizable wage. And I don’t think you have a shred of physical proof of anything beyond that<>

Suzy, having not been asked a question, chose not to respond. The courtroom is silent before Roger’s defense attorney turns and walks back to his desk.

<>No further questions your honor<> <> <> <> <> <> <> <> <> <> [[Next|Court Case Finale][$scene to _scene]]<> <>

Liz next brings up the drug bust that you took part in at Cocksleeve High School. She calls the young man up to the stand that you chased down and captured before he could escape. Liz told you that he was willing to testify against your Uncle and now that day has finally come to pass.

<>So please, tell the court who exactly hired you, and what he hired you for<> <>Mr. Condamne hired me to sell drugs in the High School. My dad owed him some money because he’s got a gambling problem. I went to try and sort it out for him. And he told me flat out to sell drugs for him at the High School, and my profit could cover my dad’s losses<> <>I’m so very sorry that you had to go through this. You’re safe now. We will do everything in our power to protect you and your father from this dastardly man<>

Liz hams it up for the jury, who seem to be listening extremely intently to this new information.

<> <> <> <> <> <> <> <> [[Next|Court Case Finale][$scene to _scene]]<> <>

The driver of the van you stopped during the human trafficking bust is called to the stand next. He still looks banged up from the incident, wearing a sling for his arm. He looks disheveled, and filed with fear in this instance.

<>This man drove a vehicle, attempting to escape with several kidnapped women in the back. Luckily, a brave man stopped his escape and all of those women are now free and home where they belong. But, to this man’s credit, he has accepted a plea deal. With his sworn testimony today, we have agreed to twenty years in prison, rather than life behind bars. So sir, please tell us exactly, who it is who hired you to transport these trafficked women<> <>It was Roger Condamne<> <>Were you told it was Mr. Condamne? Or did you meet him in person when you were hired?<> <>When I was hired I was just told it was Condamne. But during one of my deliveries, Condamne himself did come out and pay me personally<>

The testimony isn’t damning, but it is certainly swaying. The jury taking in this information in a way that does not seem good for your Uncle.

<> <> <> <> <> <> [[Next|Court Case Finale][$scene to _scene]]<> <>

Liz walks to the front of a courtroom, carrying a knife in an evidence bag. The knife responsible for the double homicide you helped investigate. The dried blood was still on the blade. It is a powerful visual for the jury’s sake.

<>This knife was used to commit a double homicide. Once committed by someone who has spent their life forced to work for Mr. Condamne mostly against their will. We have apprehended the murderer, and with her confession to this and many other crimes, we have offered her an extremely generous deal. She will testify today, and in return we will allow her to return to her home country. To be with her family. With that explanation, I will now call Sera Akumi to the stand<>

Uncle Roger’s face sinks at first. But is quickly replaced with an angry scowl as he see Sera walk up to the witness booth and sit to give testimony.

[img["ressources/scene/law/court/sera.webp"]] <>Ms. Akumi, please state for the court your nation of origin<> <>I was born in China<> <>Thank you. Now, I must ask, why are you here today? And not in China? Did you come here for greater opportunity?<> <>No. I was brought here. As a baby<> <>Was it your parents who brought you here?<> <>No. My parents were murdered by the men who brought me here<> <>I’m so very sorry to hear that. How old were you when this happened?<> <>Eight<> <>Just a child, so very tragic. Who then, may I ask, raised you after that point?<> <>Roger bought me from the men when I was nine. Raised me since then<> <>Now one might hear that and think this was a good thing. A wealthy businessman selflessly pays to take in a young woman. And raise her in a safer environment. But that isn’t the truth of it is it Sera?<> <>No. Truth is that he had me trained to kill. When I turned eighteen, he made me become an assassin for him<> <>Is that all he did?<> <>No. When I was eighteen he also began to use me sexually<> <>So, according to you, Mr. Condamne bought you from human traffickers, raised you to be a killer, and once you came of age, he set you loose on his enemies and began abusing you sexually. He treated you like an object that he purchased, rather than a person he raised or cared for. Am I right?<> <>That is correct<>

The courtroom is silent. There is a heavy air in the room as these horrible acts are put on full display for the jury to see. It is a damning testimony. And one that has no doubt swayed the hearts and minds of the Jury to look at your Uncle less favorably.

<> [[Next|Court Case Finale][$scene to 12]]<> <>

With Liz’s case made, it is now time for the defense to position their arguments. Your Uncle’s attorney stands up and gives the jury a smug smile.

<>The defense calls $mc.name $mc.surname to the stand<>

Being called to the stand so suddenly is an experience that makes your heart sink. You were not prepared for this, but this is the course of events and you need to take them in stride. You need to do all you can to show this court that your Uncle is guilty. Justice needs to be delivered. You reach the stand, and are sworn in. You take your seat and patiently wait for your Uncle’s attorney to begin his questioning.

<>Mr. $mc.surname, there have been some serious claims made in this courtroom today. Both against my client, and against you. Before I ask you any further questions, would you care to comment on any of the claims made against you? As a defense attorney, I value the opportunity to defend oneself from accusations<>

You aren’t sure how to respond at first. You look to Liz for guidance, and she gives you an extremely subtle shake of her head. You decide to tell the attorney that you have nothing you feel the need to say.

<>Nothing at all? Is that your way of saying that my client’s accusations are in fact true?<>

You deny that claim. And assert that you were not perpetrating any illegal activity.

<>So you admit that you did work for Mr. Condamne at his establishment?<>

You answer that yes, you did work there.

<>And in the course of working there, you performed jobs that were illicit in nature?<>

You again affirm that as the truth, correcting that not all were illicit or illegal. But some certainly were.

<>You admit very boldly to criminal activity, and yet you expect us to believe that the man who claims no involvement is the true perpetrator. And that you were just following his orders?<>

You say yes once more. Telling the attorney and the jury that the illegal activities were under your Uncle’s instruction, or under the instruction of someone who spoke with your Uncle’s authority.

<>Well I can assure you that no one but Mr. Condamne speaks with his authority. So now you admit that others were giving orders. Your story keeps changing how can we know you’re telling the truth? You are even admitting you are a criminal. Your lies hold no water in this court Mr. $mc.surname<>

You assert that you can told only the truth, and if he is going to say that you are lying, then he needs to be prepared to defend that claim in a defamation suit. The attorney recoils. He steps back and looks at you angrily.

<>So you admit to all of this. Saying that much of what Mr. Condamne said was true, even if not all of it. I do have to ask, was his claim of your relationship with your family true as well?<>

The courtroom is hushed while they await your reply. You say that like his other statements, that one was filled with half truths.

You explain, choosing your words very carefully, that you are in a sexual relationship with the women he named. But that these relationships are in no way incestuous, as you share no formal blood relation to any of them. Nothing that your father married $mom.name after your birth Mother died. The answer seems to make some jury members still look at you unfavorably. And other look at you with a hint of jealousy. Namely some of the men that have been checking out your mom and aunt as they sit in the pews during the trial.

<>No further questions your honor<> [[Liz cross examines you|Court Case Finale][$scene to 13]]<> <> <>Mr. $mc.surname, Can you tell the court how you and I met?<>

You tell the story of being picked up outside your Uncle’s casino and being brought into her office.

<>Thank you. I can corroborate that<>

Her cute comment gets a bit of a laugh out of the court.

<>So now can you please explain why I had you brought there? And please spare no detail. Everything about the meeting is important<>

You begin explaining the situation she was in, needing help to take your Uncle down. And then you talk about the deal she offered you. Help her get evidence against your Uncle, and she will give you immunity for all crimes committed while working for him. Liz then walks back to the desk and pulls out a signed agreement. She hands it to the judge before speaking.

<>Mr. $mc.surname has been working as an informant and sometimes aid for our department for quite some time. His actions were in service of this greater cause. As you enter the Dojo you hear the sounds of people sparring. You see Sera and another woman going at it in the ring. The girl is surprisingly strong and is going toe to toe with Sera. But, even though she puts up a good fight, Sera comes out on top in the end. At this point, you continue to believe that you might be the only person that can beat Sera in the whole city. Sera helps the defeated young lady back to her feet just as you approach them both.

<><>. This is Ember. A friend<> <>Hey hey. A friend of Sera’s is a friend of mine. Nice to meet ya!<> [img["ressources/scene/sera/emberintro.webp"]]

You shake Ember’s hand as you greet her. You ask them how they know each other, noting that you have spent a lot of time with Sera recently but don’t remember running into Ember at any point before.

<>Oh we go wayyyyyy back. But I’m super busy these days. I work at City Hall for Mayor Tanaka. So I don’t get to come around as often as I’d like<>

You are kinda of shocked that someone who works the City’s government would come here and be okay with some of the activities that go on. You even start to get worried about talking to Ember. But she and Sera assuage your worries rather quickly.

<>She can be trusted<> <>Oh yeah I know all about this stuff. She’d never admit it but the Mayor kinda does too. And what is government besides just one big old Mafia anyway?<>

Ember’s laughter is mildly obnoxious. But her upbeat attitude manages to be infectious none the less. You ask them both if they’re done training, or if they have time for you to join in and get some work in. They look at one another. Almost like they know something that you don’t.

<>I have an Idea. Spar with us both<> <>Yeah, Sera told me you beat her. I hardly believe it but I wanna see how tough you really are. Fight us both at once!<>

You tell them you’ll almost definitely lose that fight. Two on one is hardly fair.

<>Well duh. But if you win we can have some fun<> <>She means sex<> <>Sera! Jeez learn what subtlety is<>

You laugh at the proposition. But figure it would be worth losing a fight to take the chance of winning and getting to fuck them both. And the worst case scenario is that you lose and get some good training work out of it. So the risk is minimal at worst. You tell the ladies you agree to the terms, and tell them to get ready to fight. Sera gives you a knowing smile as she goes to the far corner of the sparring mat, leading Ember there along with her.

[[Get ready to rumble|Sera Stage 4][$scene to 0; $sera.questmain to 4; $sera.gallery[3] to 1]]<> <>

Your training with Sera, and on your own, have been paying off. You feel strong, fast, and ready to take on almost any challenge these days. It’s no wonder to you why Sera spends so much time training. And it’s no surprise that when you visit the Dojo to see her, she is already busy training. Just as she does every day.

She has her hands wrapped in tape and she is working on her technique with a wooden sparring dummy. The dummy is covered in chips and dents in the wood. It is well worn in and shows just how hard Sera can actually hit as well. Every time she strikes it, you are amazed that she doesn’t split it apart with the force of her strikes. You wait for her to finish up before approaching. She wears a scowl on her face as you approach. Something she often does when training. You decide to ask her if she’s alright, hoping to get a little closer to her.

<>I am fine. Why do you ask?<>

She seemed genuinely confused by the question. As if she had no idea that she scowls when she trains. So you explain it to her. Telling her that when she is training, she looks so angry and unhappy. And you just wanted to know why that is, or if there is something you could do to alleviate the anger.

<>Oh,.. Thank you for the offer. I am okay. I just release anger through my strikes. My face must release it too. Apologies if it bothered you<>

Sera suddenly seemed so meek in that moment. As if she was being scorned. You assure her that you weren’t bothered at all. Correcting that you were making sure that she wasn’t bothered.

<>I am never bothered<>

You could tell she was lying. You could tell that there was something on her mind that prevented her from telling you exactly why she wouldn’t talk about her frustrations. But you could see on her face that nothing you could say would make her explain it in this moment. But you thought that there might be something that you could do. So you ask her to spar with you, telling her that you want to go all out this time. So you can really test your strength and progress in your training. She almost looks concerned when hearing that you want to go all out.

<>Are you certain? I could hurt you<>

You push out some smarmy confidence and say that you could hurt her too. Something that elicits a genuine laugh from Sera. One of the first you’ve ever seen from her. She shrugs and moves to the corner of the sparring ring.

<>Do not say I did not tell you so<> [[Let’s get ready to rumble|Sera Stage 3][$scene to 0; $sera.questmain to 3; $sera.gallery[2] to 1]]<> <>

You’re ready to step up your training to the next level. You head into the Dojo and see that Sera is working on her blade skills at the moment. The idea to ask her for some weapons training sparks in your mind the moment you see her. You walk up to her and greet her, asking her if she is up for some training today. She finishes a flurry of strikes with her blade against a dummy made out of a canvass wrapping filled with straw and stuck on a wooden pole.

<>I always am. What do you want to train?<>

She is blunt and almost emotionless, like always. You wish that you could get her to say more. You wish she would give you even a little bit of insight on how she is feeling. But for now, you’ll keep on working to grow closer to her and earn her trust. Someone like her is much better as an ally than not. And allies are the only way you advance in the criminal underworld.

You answer Sera’s question, pointing to her sword and telling her that if she could train you in how to handle some weapons properly. She looks at her blade for a moment, sheathes it, and then walks over to you. She nods in understanding, then points to the wall where several bamboo training swords are hanging. Clearly indicating to you that she wants you to get them and bring them over. You grab a wooden sword for yourself and for Sera, handing it to her when you return to the mat with them both.

<>Rule one, never give your opponent a weapon<>

She snaps the wooden blade against your shin suddenly to drive the point home. You rub the sore spot on your leg for a moment. The point she made is valid but the way she made it was undeniably obnoxious. But, obnoxious is more emotion than nothing so you feel like you are at least getting somewhere with her.

You proceed, more so on your toes that before as she begins to teach you how to properly wield a weapon in a fight. Everything from proper grip, to where to aim, and how to protect yourself when you strike. You go back and forth for a while, and she remains clearly superior to you with weapons. But in time you do show improvement, even managing to land a strike on her. She smiles at you when you do, in an almost proud way. Something that throws you off guard long enough for her to counter attack you.

<>You still have much to learn. But you have done well. Come with me, progress deserves reward. Just as failure deserves punishment<> [[Follow Sera to her room|Sera Stage 2][$scene to 0; $sera.questmain to 2; $sera.gallery[1] to 1]]<> <>

Sera Akumi spends much of her day training in her Dojo. On occasion, she will be sparring or fighting someone. And it is very rare that she even comes close to losing. You figure that it is a good idea to know how to fight considering the dangers of working for an organization like your Uncle’s. So, you head to the Dojo to see if Sera would mind teaching you a few things. She is stretching her body in some yoga pants and a sports bra that really hug her figure nicely. It is almost enough to distract you but her rather cold and matter of fact nature snaps you out of the trance her body puts you under.

You step closer until you’re right in front of her, and she looks at you expectantly. You tell her that you were hoping that she could teach you a few things. Explaining that you wanna be good at fighting to defend yourself. She nods in understanding.

<>This is good. I will help. Step into the ring. Show me your skill<>

You do as she says, stepping into the makeshift arena that is set up in the Dojo. Sera enters from the other side. She readies herself, and you do the same. She watches you patiently, clearly waiting for you to make a move. You don’t want to waste her time so you lunge, going after her and throwing a punch towards her chest. You don’t hold back, knowing that if anyone can handle a hit, it would be her.

But, you don’t come close to landing. She spins and knocks your fist away with ease. She throws two jabs of her own at you. One at your ribs, and one at your knee. You buckle and drop instantly. The jabs didn’t hurt particularly badly. Dropping onto the mat hurt worse. That and the hit to your pride. You pop back up quickly though, showing that you won’t stay down.

You nod in understanding, and then make your next move. She deflects you again. This dance goes on for some time. Eventually you manage to graze her shoulder with a punch. It isn’t much but it is a landed hit. One that does seem to surprise her.
