She needs to understand that life is about give and take. If she isn’t willing to be kind and professional with other staff and especially with superiors, then she will never hold down a job for long.

<>I can give! I promise I can give<>

Wylla suddenly starts undressing. You try to stop her, but that just makes her cry harder.

<>Why won’t you let me give?<>

Everything is getting confusing now. She’s naked, and taking off your pants. You weren’t trying to get sex out of her. But either she thought that you were, or she has some twisted mentality that this can be how she gives, to allow her to take. It’s a lot to process, especially when she starts riding your cock. Bouncing her ass on you hard and fast. But… at least she stopped crying.

[[Continue|Wylla Stage 3 Sub]]<> <>

It's time to decide how to deal with Wylla. This choice will determine her route.

[[Threaten Wylla with firing again|Wylla Stage 2 Sub][$scene to 0]] <>[[Show Wylla who’s boss|Wylla Stage 2 Dom][$scene to 0]]<>
Show Wylla who’s boss (Need at least 5 dominance)<> <>

The sound of arguing coming from the boardroom is a bit more heated than anything you’ve heard coming from here before. It’s hard to make out at first. But you get a pretty good idea of what it’s about when you see Susan storming out. She doesn’t even pay attention to you as she storms past into the elevator. You head in and see Levi flipping through some of his papers. The lack of emotion on his face says that he is either unphased by it all. Or he is very good at hiding his anger. You greet him once you walk in.

<>Hello to you too, Mr. Chairman<>

You take a seat at the table, and ask Levi what the yelling was about. You are genuinely curious, but you make it sound like you are making casual conversation with him.

<>Oooh just more of Dr. Bellows crying and raving about salaries. It can be so frustrating to explain the reality of financials to someone, one hundred different ways, without ever getting through to them<>

You aren’t intimately familiar with the financials of the Hospital either. So you explain that and ask what is actually keeping them from putting more into the staff.

<>It’s isn’t as much as the money isn’t there at all. But as I’ve explained to Dr. Bellows, increasing wages is a bad investment<>

A bad investment? You ask him why paying good staff is a bad investment.

<>Because there is no direct return. The doctor already works for us, and does a good job for what we pay them. None of them are going to suddenly perform better if we pay them more. And they all care too much to perform worse if we don’t. So let me ask you, do you think I should spend ten percent of our budget on raises that won’t make the hospital any better than it currently is? Paying more to them year after year. Or, should I spend that on one time purchases of equipment? Equipment that will make them better by virtue of better tools and technology at their disposal! Or better yet, supplies that we get profit from through insurance payments<>

You tell him that you see his point. But not that it’s a rather callous one to make. There is something admirable about wanting better for your fellow employees.

<>Oh I completely agree Mr. Chairman. But handling the budget isn’t about being admired. It’s about making the tough decisions that keep this place running and funded. If only Dr. Bellows would stop to think about that for just a moment<>

You ask him what would he think if the doctors left to work at other hospitals. Wouldn’t it be worth paying them more to keep them?

<>No, no. While I understand why that though comes to mind, you need to consider a couple things<>

The arrogance in his tone is annoying to sit through. It’s easy to see why Susan gets so frustrated with him.

<>First, we pay our doctors well. They aren’t going hungry. In fact we pay above the average market rate in the city. It will be tough for them to even find a job that pay them as much as we do. Let alone more. And the second is that if they would threaten to leave over a small bump in pay, then I say it’s addition by subtraction. Greedy people have no place in the medical field<>

You take a moment to relish in the unwitting hypocrisy of his own statement just now. Levi does have decent arguments for why he doesn’t raise the pay. But they are undoubtedly scummy. And not the type of mindset you want for this hospital going forward. Replacing Levi is going to go a long way towards enacting your vision. And Susan might be just the person to speak to about getting rid of him.

[[Go find Susan|Susan Stage 2][$scene to 0]]<> <>

The TV in the board room is set up with Hilda connecting her laptop to it. She smiles at you when she sees you walk in. Today is finally the day that she seems ready to present her counter proposal to you as well as the rest of the board. You’re the first to arrive, as usual. Giving you a few moments to talk with her before everyone else arrives. You ask her if she’s certain she’s ready for this.

<>Absolutely. I’ve been considering some of these changes before I even became Chief of Medicine. So, thank you for finally giving me a good opportunity to present these ideas. Compared to some of yours, they’ll look less radical. And they might actually get passed<>

She has an almost smug confidence about her. It makes you chuckle inside knowing that it will still almost certainly get shot down with little support. You tell her, that out of fairness, both you and her should abstain from this vote. So personal opinions don’t interfere in the process.

<>Okay, I can agree to that. Just so long as you do the same if you present your ideas again in the future<>

It’s a fair request. So you agree. Just then the others begin to file into the room one after another. Before long the entire board has arrived and is ready. Hilda leads the processions, moving through old business and into new quickly to get to her presentation.

<>After $mc.name’s proposal at one of our previous meetings, it raised several questions to me about the future of this hospital. While we mostly agreed that his proposal was too radical, I believe we all also agreed that change was warranted<>

She looks at the board, being reminded that not all of them are the same as they were when you first made your proposal.

<>Well, at least all of the members at that time agreed that change was warranted. So I’ve prepared a proposal of my own<>

She clicks through slides, showcasing her plan. And even providing data from other hospitals around the nation to back up the ideas.

<>With a more structured pay scaling, we can ensure budget stability while also raising the average wages of our doctors and nurses<>

Many of her ideas are similar. Suggestions that are meant to give good results to most people, but will inevitably end up harming a few in the process. It has a very maximize benefit while ignoring the additional harming aftershocks feel to the presentation as a whole. It’s logical, but ultimately heartless. And the rest of the board clearly agrees. The moment she is done, she calls for a vote. And as votes come in, her face sinks.

<> <>Considering this plan would mean cutting my own salary, I’m sorry Hilda but I have to vote No<> <> <>You wanna punish the competent doctors and just make pay the same across the board? Are you fucking dumb? No from me<> <> <>I really don’t think this is as fair as you thought it is. A really good doctor might not work here because somewhere else offers more. My sister always taught me that the economics matter and this is bad economics<> <><> <>I haven’t donated money to this hospital for decades just to have it keep changing. I vote no, and will always vote no<> <> <>I don’t see how this helps anyone but you, Hilda. It doesn’t help any of us at all. It just makes you look good for getting your ideas approved. It’s a no from me<> <> <>I think you can do better than this Hilda. Patients won’t like this and at the end, unless we all benefit, them being unsatisfied does more harm than good for us. I’m voting no<> <> <>I’m voting no. The opinion at the table clearly is adversarial to this. I can’t really side with something so unpopular. It would be pointless<> <><> <>This is a much improved plan but the financials still just don’t support this. I don’t think I can find the money to support this. I’ll be voting no<> <> <>You want to spend how much? Oh, no no. That’s just way too much Hilda. I vote no.<> <> <>Do you see how expensive this would be? If you’re gonna try and bankrupt us, don’t do it for a half-assed idea. I’m voting no on this crap<> <> <>It’s clear that you don’t know mathematics as well as I do. If you did, you would see that this hospital plainly doesn’t have enough money to support your plan. I would think simple addition wouldn’t be too difficult. But here we are. I’m not going to support this<> <><> <>I don’t even have time to point out how many legal issues this opens us up to. You’d be an idiot to try and push this through. No way I vote in favor of this<> <> <>I could go on for hours noting the amount of poorly phrased, vague, loophole generating language you’ve used in this presentation. But as we only have a short time to discuss this I will hold off on that and just write out a detailed criticism instead. In short though, I will be voting no. Please expect my many reasons to follow soon<> <> <>Have you considered how the Traditionalists will react to this? They will be livid. And don’t get me started on the Protectionists. No no, this won’t do. I have to vote against this. The public response would be terrible<> <>

The color drains from Hilda’s face as she realizes how definitively she has been voted down. Her face goes slightly red from a mix of anger and embarrassment. She clearly thought that she would get at least one vote in the process of all of this. And as she brings the board meeting to an end, she slowly lists away to her office. Looking defeated and likely feeling even worse. You wait for everyone else to file out before leaving as well. Hilda should probably have a moment to collect her thoughts before you go and speak to her about holding up her end of the arrangement.

[[Continue|Hospital Board][$hilda.questmain to 3.1]]<> <>

Wylla is taking Archibald’s blood pressure. You wouldn’t have walked in on it by choice. But considering she is doing it for him in the middle of the board room, you didn’t have much in the way of warning about it. When they see you, Wylla finishes up what she’s doing and writes some information down in a chart. She turns to you and gives you a playful smile, before walking past you to leave. Practically teasing you.

[img["ressources/scene/hospital/board/wylla.webp"]] <>She is a firecracker isn’t she?<>

His comment makes you realize that he was staring at Wylla’s ass the entire time she was walking out. You can’t blame him. You’ve seen her ass. It’s a nice view. But him being three, or maybe even four times her age just makes it unbearably creepy. Not wanting to discuss it with him, you change the subject right away. Asking if he is alright, and wondering why she was taking his blood pressure.

<>Can’t be too careful at my age. And especially not after three heart attacks. But if you wanna know why Wylla is doing it, it’s because the other nurses hate when I pinch their behinds. Wylla just pinches me back<>

That’s a mental image that you could have done without.

<>We need more nurses like her. Maybe then this hospital would be more worth my money. Too many nurses here are sensitive. They need to lighten up and have fun like the old days. Ahhh even if they don’t, I could never give this place up. Too many hot pieces of tail come through every day<>

You tease that if they did that he might just get overwhelmed by the nurses and sent into another heart attack.

<>No better time to have one then, right?<>

He cracks up at his own joke. The laughter quickly turning into sickly coughs. You laugh politely, feeling a bit turned off by how sick it actually sounds. Telling him that you have to go for now. But you’ll see him at the next board meeting.

<>I’m sure, I’m sure<>

As you leave, the thought that you need to get this man out of his position comes back to the forefront of your mind. Hell with how old he is, it almost feels like its your responsibility to push him into retirement. He’s never gonna leave on his own, he basically told you as much just a moment ago. So going after his health might be the only choice you really have. How you do that though, is the question.

[[Continue|Hospital Board][$hospital.board.donor.setup to 1; $wylla.gallery[13] to 1]]<> <> <>Ya know Elliot, I just don’t think you’re understanding me. The settlement offer we made is non-negotiable… And there you go trying to negotiate again! I’m starting to wonder if I’m speaking Greek. I’m not? Good, then do us both a favor and call me back when you remember what non-negotiable means<>

You walk in just as the Hospital’s Lawyer is finishing up another call. It’s seemed rather heated so you ask him if everything’s alright. He only looks at you for a moment to acknowledge your existences before looking back at his phone.

<>It will be. Lawyers can be stubborn. I know because I know myself. So sometimes I need to play a little hardball. Otherwise people won’t get their heads out of their asses. It’s all in the best interest of the hospital. Especially when a lawyer can’t help but try and negotiate<>

Hardball sounds a bit like the nice way to phrase strong arming people. Nothing necessarily wrong with that. But it does indicate that Michael would be more than willing to blur lines of legal ethics. Even if you weren’t already trying to get the members of the Board replaced, this would be a concerning quality. You ask him another question, one to parse out if he is someone who blurs the line. Or if maybe he’s someone who would cross it. You ask him why not just skip the lawyer and go right to the client if their lawyer keeps blowing up the agreement with counter offers. He doesn’t even skip a beat with his answer.

<>That’s illegal. Opposing council can’t contact a client in a case without their lawyer present. But, we can make sure they know what we want them to know. Sometimes someone we have on retainer, like a private investigator, will just happen to run into the people we want them too. Maybe share a little gossip<>

You nod to show him that you get what he’s saying. It’s clear that he will cross boundaries. But even worse, he’s done it enough to be smart about it. It won’t be easy to work Michael out of his position. But this conversation has at least given you a few ideas on how you might be able to do it. You thank him for humoring your questions.

<>Not at all. You’re as much my client as a member of this Board as the rest. And I’m already here so, the time was billable either way. Have a good day, Mr. $mc.surname<>

Michael leaves, walking with a swagger that annoys you even with him technically being on your side. The sooner you replace him, the better. You don’t need snakes in this hospital.

[[Continue|Hospital Board][$hospital.board.lawyer.setup to 1]]<> <> [[Propose a new hospital rule|Hospital Board Rules][$step to 1]] [[Talk to the board members|Hospital Board Members]] [[Leave|Hospital Admin Floor]] <>

passages.name: Hospital Board Departure
passages.source_raw:
<> <>

Thomas walks into the boardroom and takes a seat across from you. He looks tired as he always has. And a little bit annoyed that you called him here to speak with him. So you start this off by thanking him for coming. Acknowledging that you know he’s busy so you won’t take much of his time.

<>Get to it. The platitudes are just time wasters themselves<>

You nod in understanding. Not wasting any time before coming out and explaining exactly why you called him here. You’d like him to retire. A request that makes him scoff.

<>Why the hell would I do that?<>

The tiredness in his eyes and voice is easy to notice. And you bring up what Thomas said to you previously. How hard it hits him every single time. You see how much it wears on him. And for the good of himself, and the hospital, you think it would be best if he moves on and rests.

<>Don’t act like you know me. And don’t act like you’re doing me some sort of favor. If I could retire, I would. But I got too many years left, and too many things to pay for too retire now<>

Retiring is a hard barrier to step over. Going from having a job to having none, it creates an instant feeling of insecurity. But between his pension, and social security, Thomas would have no issues retiring today. You don’t say that though. It’s rude to presume what his financial situation truly is. The simple solution though, is the one that you came into this room prepared to offer. A bribe, though you don’t phrase it as one. You offer Thomas a nest egg. Ten years of his salary in one lump sum, as a gift. To make his transition to retirement easier.

<>You wanna give me that much, just to retire? This a bribe? You trying to get rid of me?<>

The simple answer is yes. Not for any malicious reason but, because you’re worried that he has become jaded. And that it would be better to have someone with a more positive outlook to be the chief of surgery. And you wouldn’t want to make this suggestion without respecting what he’s done for the hospital and the medical field in general. Which is why you want to offer him this money. To push him out the door with dignity rather than have him run the risk of him wearing down and leaving too late. Your explanation doesn’t seem to move Thomas one way or the other. But he is clearly considering it heavily.

<>Give me it in writing, and it’s a deal<>

You nod with a slight smile. Telling him you’ll have the paperwork over to him by the end of the day. He gets up and leaves without another word. Doesn’t seem like he’s too happy about it. But as long as he’s content, then he leaves. And him leaving is the goal. One spot is now open on this board. Open for you to fill. Just as you hoped it would be when you came in here today.

''Thomas Dunn has left the board!''<> <>

Thomas needs to go. After how he acted back in the hallway, you now know that he is nothing but an aging and stubborn guy. Too set in his ways to be convinced to reasoned with. And too stubborn to bother trying anything else to get him to leave other than forcing him out. He’s rather well respected among the staff and Board. So forcing him out is going to require some pretty drastic measures. Luckily, you have just the brat to get under his skin. And hopefully, under his pants too. You call $sis.name and ask her to stop by the hospital. You make sure to tell her that it isn’t because anyone is hurt. You just need to speak to her in the board room. She shows up not long after. Seeming happy to just have an excuse to get out and do something.

<>Hey <>$sis.title<>$mc.name<>! What do ya need? And reaaally take your time telling me too. I wanna make sure I can listen completely<>

You tease her, saying that you won’t take long. She has homework that needs to be done. You know it just by how happy she is to not be at home working on it. And you’re going to make sure she does it. An assurance that makes her pout slightly.

<>Fine. What did you want anyway?<>

The plan is simple. She needs to seduce someone for you.

<>You want me to go fuck some guy? What for?<>

As crude as she put it, she is right. The reason, as you explain it to her, is that she needs to play the role of the homewrecker. The man she is going to seduce is someone you don’t like much. And with his reputation destroyed, you’ll be able to do some good for this hospital.

<> <>Yes $sis.title. Anything you ask of me<> <> <>I guess I’ll take care of it. You owe me though!<> <>

Your sister walks out. Set on completing her task. It doesn’t take long for her to complete it either. You don’t ask for details. You don’t really want them. All that matters to you is that it happened and the ‘secret’ gets out. And it gets out in a much more substantial way than you previously could have guessed. $sis.name filmed the whole thing. And now it’s out there for the whole world to see. Dr. Dunn, cheating on his wife.

The rest of the plan goes by without a hitch. Thomas resigns in shame. His reputation ruined, his marriage dissolved, and his place on the board is left open. He didn’t even resign in person. He just sent the entire board an email. You doubt you’ll ever hear from him again.

''Thomas Dunn has left the board!''<><> <>

If Michael is willing to skirt the line so brazenly that he would openly admit to it in front of you, then there is no doubt in your mind that behind closed door he is likely crossing that line. Even if you didn’t have an ulterior motive, an investigation into his conduct is surely warranted. You call in one of the administrators of the state’s bar association, Tim Powell, for a quick chat. He arrives at your office at City Hall just when you asked him too.

[img["ressources/scene/hospital/board/tim.webp"]] <>Mayor $mc.surname, glad to have gotten your call. What can I help you with today?<>

You explain your predicament. Saying that while you don’t wish to accuse him of anything directly, you’re aware that Michael Black is acting extremely unethically. And you wonder if there is anything Tim can do about that.

<>Now that is concerning. Trouble is, without proof, it will be hard to pull his license. We could bring him up on review, call it an anonymous tip. But that won’t last long. He would be questioned, and likely just let off with a warning at best<>

You wonder aloud if there were possibly a way to have the bar look at minor infractions with more scrutiny. Tim’s eyes go wide for a moment. Then he begins to nod slowly.

<>With the right incentives, I’m sure several members of the ethics committee could be swayed to take a more hard-line approach to ethics<>

It’s wonderful news to hear. You have plenty of incentives to offer. With Tim’s aid, you grease the right palms throughout the bar association. And in short order, Michael Black is brought before the ethic committee on so many minor charges that they effectively combine into one massive charge. He did nothing illegal, so he has little to worry about in that regard. But he has certainly done enough questionable things that quickly came to light during this review, that his license was indefinitely revoked. He can no longer be the hospital’s in house council when he can no longer practice law in the state. The moment that committee voted, that spot opened up on the hospital board. And now it’s up to you to decide who to fill it with.

''Michael Black has been removed from the board!''<> <> <>You wanted to see me?<>

You called Susan in after you heard about a case coming against the hospital soon. It came through the grapevine that the patient she yelled at the same day that you first met her, is suing her over the encounter. It’s a frivolous suit, and even if it is successful it would be very cheap to pay the penalties for. But the money isn’t what you’re concerned with. You’re focused on getting Michael out of his position and seat on the Board. And having him lose such a meaningless case is the perfect justification to use to get rid of him. With Susan in the board room with you, you explain that you’d like her to be completely honest and upfront about anything and everything that occurred on that day. You know that Michael will coach her to be more coy with her wording. But in an effort more transparency you request that she not take any of that coaching on. At least, transparency is the reason you provide for her. She doesn’t need to know the truth.

<>Totally honest? Fine, I’ll be sure to tell that worm how pathetic he is for even bringing up this suit<>

Her response couldn’t be more perfect. She heads out and then, all you have to do is wait. Depositions come around, and when Susan says what she truly thinks, and tells the full truth, Michael’s chances of winning the case plummet. And the anger of the former patient skyrockets. Michael tries all he can to settle out of court. But he fails completely. And then, he loses. It’s actually impressive how well Michael does in the case considering how stacked against him it is. But with such an embarrassing loss on his record, you have all the justification you need to have him fired and removed from the Board. But the best part about it, is that you don’t even need to fire him. He opts to resign instead. Likely trying to hold on to the last shred of dignity that he can muster after this disaster.

Now that he’s gone though, your focus shifts. He has a seat that needs to be filled. And you need to fill it with someone loyal to you.

''Michael Black has been removed from the board!''<><> <> <>I will do it<> [img[ressources/scene/hospital/board/sera.webp]]

You’re confused, you haven’t even had the chance to explain what you want Sera to do for you yet. You only just called her over to speak with her. But you hadn’t even told her that it was over your plan to remove Archibald from the Board yet.

<>You are my <>$sera.title<>Don<>. My loyalty, is yours. There is little you can do, that I do not see. I am always watching<>

Normally someone telling you that they’re always watching would be incredibly creepy. And this time isn’t much different. But, there is something about Sera herself, that makes it just barely comforting. Maybe it’s because you are certain of her loyalty, so it helps you trust her motives more. You decide to diffuse the tension created by what she said with a bit of teasing. Asking her that if she is so sure, then she should lay out what you called her there for herself.

<>You want me to end the presence of a member of this Board. The elderly one<>

You nod. She is entirely right. Which really only serve to make what she said a moment ago even more unsettling. She is about to leave, clearly planning to waste no time. But you stop her. Telling her to do her best to make it appear as though his age got the better of him. The less possible incrimination the better.

<>Yes <>$sera.title<>Don<>. I will do as you ask. No one will know, but you and I<>

Sera leaves the hospital immediately. And you sit back and wait for the news. It doesn’t come for a while. But a simple text telling you that the job is completed comes in eventually. And that’s all you need to see. It won’t be long before the news of his passing gets out. Something that will be sad, but will be rather expected at this very late stage of his life. And now, it’s time to consider who shall take his place.

''Archibald Lewiston has left the Board!''<><> <>

As you consider ways to remove Archibald from the Board, you become increasingly curious of just how he got his way onto it in the first place. You presume that it was by basically buying a spot, similar to how you got there. But just where did his money come from? You’ve never heard of him before. No companies with his name on it, or one with a history of him leading them. And usually shrewd market traders get some sort of notoriety that you would have heard of by now. Yet when you look into Archibald, you quickly see why you haven’t heard of him before. His wealth has absolutely nothing to do with this city. It takes a while to find but you see that Archibald is listed as the owner of thousands of acres of property a few states a way. Acres that are all leased by farmers and ranchers. He makes millions in passive income every year. And with how many years he’s been around, you can’t imagine just how much he might have earned over all that time. But it does give you a clear path on how to hurt those finances of his. Those farms rely on stores and businesses, primarily within Seaside, to buy what they produce. If you make it so enough of those businesses buy elsewhere, those farms will have to move on to somewhere new, because they just won’t find buyers nearby that can justify the prices.

All it takes is the right businesses to buy. A few stock purchases here and there, mixed with a forced change of direction with the companies, is all it takes to create serious instability within the market. This isn’t an instant solution. Archibald will have the money to withstand this sort of manipulation in the short term. But you aren’t trying to just bankrupt the man. You’re goal is to stress him out. And it clearly works. After your many moves, it isn’t too long before you get an email from Hilda. She informs the entire Board that health concerns have led to Archibald resigning from the Board. Perhaps just a cover to save face from his financial fears. At least you hope that he didn’t have a heart attack over it all. Either way, his seat is open. And now you just need to figure out who you plan on filling it with.

''Archibald Lewiston has left the Board!''<> <> [[Continue|Hospital Board Members]]<>

passages.name: Hospital Board First Meeting
passages.source_raw:
<>

Just then a very chipper man strolls into the room. He looks extremely nerdy, despite his obviously expensive suit. His thick glasses are the biggest draw on his appearance. His eye look like saucers by how much they’re magnified.

[img["ressources/scene/hospital/board/accounts.webp"]] <>Goooood morning all<> <>Tone it down a bit Levi. My head is killing me<> <>Oops, sorry Thomas. I’ll try<> <>New suit, Levi? Is that why you’re so chipper?<> <>You always see right through me Hilda. It sure is! It’s Italian. The inside is silk too. Feels like I’m being hugged by an angel<> [[Two persons arrive|Hospital Board First Meeting][$scene to 1]]<> <>

The third and fourth board members come in together. A young but determined looking gentlemen striding in with purpose. With an older and downright rickety man following slowly behind them.

[img["ressources/scene/hospital/board/lawyer.webp"]] [img["ressources/scene/hospital/board/donor.webp"]] <>Let’s keep today short if we can. I have to be in court later today<> <>Don’t rush us Michael. We have a new member today. He should get a good look at how things operate<> <>Thank you for mentioning that Archibald. As you are all aware, $mc.name has been made chairman of this Board of Trustees<> <>Yeah, I remember the vote about him strong arming you for the position<> <>That aside, we are all grateful for his help with our funding, and are happy to have him lead this Board. $mc.name is there anything you’d like to say before we begin?<> [[Introduce yourself|Hospital Board First Meeting][$scene to 2]]<> <>

You stand up and thank Hilda. After a promise to make it quick, you introduce yourself. Explaining that you chose to help this hospital because you see potential in it. And a city can only be elevated when it’s healthcare is exemplary. You have plans to make it the top hospital not only in the city, but in the nation. But you take a seat and end it there for now, with a thank you for their welcome. Knowing that they have other business to cover first.

<>Inspiring words. Let’s not waste time then for Michael’s sake. Any old business that needs to be settled from our last meeting?<> <>I’d like to revisit the hiring freeze<> <>I’ll stop you right there Thomas. I’m still in near constant contact with Doctor Bellows. She has been hounding me for raises already. We need to squash that issue before we even think about hiring more doctors<> <>Hiring more doctors would be great leverage against raising their salary. And would make it less likely that any of them leave when there are plenty of people to replace them<> <>I appreciate your insight Thomas but I handle the financials. Not you. I know what this hospital can afford. And at this time, we cannot afford it<> <>Surely with our recent influx you can make something work<> <>This influx is nice but we need to consider the return on investment. If we increase salaries by even five percent we’re talking about millions every year. Whatever she has must be pretty serious if she’s going this far. You ask what it’s all about as she returns to her desk. She takes a deep breath, as if she is about to unload the weight of the world from her shoulders. She hands you a large manila folder with some papers inside. You begin to read through them as she explains.

<>Levi is embezzling. He doesn’t care about return on investment. He doesn’t care about getting us new equipment. He just cares that he can skim off the top. I knew something wasn’t adding up. He always talks about how he could spend the money on better things for the hospital. But outside of major purchases like a new MRI machine here and there, we haven’t gotten new equipment in so long. Our vital monitors are from the early 2000’s<>

You read through the papers, and you can’t help but agree with her conclusion. There are a few order forms here that are filled out and signed by Levi, but none of them have a receipt to go with them. And you remember how well he dresses. He’s just an accountant he shouldn’t be making enough to afford some of the suits he wears. Not with how expensive it is to live in a city like Seaside. But, all of this amounts to being circumstantial at best. Worthy of questioning, sure. But not enough to fully accuse someone of a crime like this. And you explain as much to Susan, who does not like that answer much.

<>Come on it’s so obvious a blind person would see it! Do NOT tell me you’re just going to back out when we have something so horrible as this on him!<>

You put your hand up to try and calm her down. Telling her that you have no intention of backing down. But you likely only get one real shot at removing Levi from the Board. If you go after him with this, and it fails, they will be stuck with him.

<>Please, I know Hilda. This will convince her. Just please trust me on this, if you have her on your side there is no way the others don’t follow on this. She will be livid just seeing these order forms with no receipts. What do I need to do to convince you?<>

That last question is what you really needed to hear. Having Susan support you as well in your effort to reform the hospital will be very beneficial. She may not be on the Board but she has plenty of sway among the employees here. So you explain that if she wants you to take this to the Board without something more concrete, then in return she needs to promise her loyalty to you and your plans for the hospital in the future. You’re taking a risk, and without some serious guarantees of loyalty that can help you, it just isn’t worth it.

<>Absolutely. If you get rid of Levi, and get my residents the raises the deserve, then anything you wanna implement will have my full unquestioned support. You can absolutely count on me. And I’m going to prove it, right here, right now<>

You don’t even need to ask her how she plans to do that. Susan has a very clear sense of what a show of loyalty is. Either that or she just assumes that you prefer sexual favors. You nod at her. As if to acknowledge what she said so she can continue. But she doesn’t. So you ask her plainly if it was just the office itself she wanted you to see or if there was something about it that was important to her.

<>I want you to see the size. The Chief Resident before me had an office three times as big as this. But I gave that up for an extra on call room. This is cheaper to clean and maintain<>

She looks at you as if you’re supposed to simply understand what she is implying with all of this. It isn’t readily apparent why she would want a smaller office. Giving the residents an extra on call room is certainly kind of her. It’s selfless and you commend her for that. But the purpose of her flexing this to you still alludes you.

She seems to have a point about Levi. And who knows, maybe that might just be a good thread to follow for getting him off the Board. But you can’t say any of that to her. Instead you play diplomatic. She says with a flirty smile. Susan turns and walks away, strutting away in a fashion that is clearly designed to entice you. Every piece of you is telling you to walk after her. But you restrain yourself. Taking a deep breath, and getting back to what you were doing.

She storms past you and starts looking through a filing cabinet in the nurses station. She turns back to you over her shoulder and sees you looking at her with your shocked expression.


[img["ressources/scene/alex/intro/alex.webp"]]

<>Stop staring at me, asshole<>

You apologize for staring, but continue by chiding her for screaming and her coarse language.

You introduce yourself to her properly. Telling her your name and explaining that you are the new Chairman of the Board of Trustees. Her expression doesn’t change as she slams the file cabinet shut. You chuckle at that response with a hint of disbelief at how she is acting. But you correct her. Saying that usually what people are supposed to do is introduce themselves in return. Every word that you utter is dripping with sarcasm.

Patient care is one of the most important aspects of being a doctor. And if her bedside manner is always this atrocious you wonder how she hasn’t been fired already. And you say as much to her. If your vision for this hospital can ever come to fruition, then she needs to be retaught how to treat patients like people and not like verbal punching bags. <>

There has to be a reason why he’s still around, considering how much the job is wearing on him. Maybe it’s money. Salaries are a constant topic around the hospital. It’s hard to imagine it being any good for helping patients considering it’s current layout.

You step out and find a directory on the wall. Telling you exactly where the Chief of Medicine’s office is. You follow the directions and arrive there pretty quickly. They aren’t needed, you just want to have the meeting and be on your way. As much as you appreciate the offer, you didn’t become mayor just to get tours of hospitals. You did it to get things done.

<>Focused on action. I love that. I won’t beat around the bush then. $city.name General is in need of more funding. Several of our machines need replacing. And I’m sure I don’t need to tell you how expe-<>

You cut her off. Saying that funding is a decision left to city council. It isn’t something you can unilaterally decide.

You share in her excitement at first. But when you see a good moment to bring it up, you pretend like you just noticed something bad. You act like you’re just seeing this now as you point out to her that she had the nip slip in the video. A reality that has her sounding mortified.

<>They can see my WHAT? No you have to take it down!<>

You ask her if she is sure. Saying that she would lose what is sure to be her highest rated video in the history of her channel.

<>People don’t watch me for my body. We can just cut out the nip slip and reupload it right?<>

You say that you could. But you first spend the moment to correct her that you don’t think she is right that no one watches for her body. Since she brought it up herself you think its the perfect time to let her know that the stats clearly indicate that when she dresses in more revealing clothing, she gets more views. You put it as delicately as you can. Because you know being told that people watch her for her looks isn’t something she is going to like to hear.

<>NO! I don’t believe you. It has to be a coincidence<>

You understand her denial in the moment but you reiterate that you went through the videos several times. And assure her that there truly isn’t any other visible factor. Ending with the suggestion that if she wants to bolster her view count, then going with some more risque clothing choices might be what is best for her channel.

<>I’m not going to dress like some slut for views! I don’t need to. I’ll show you. Edit the videos how I want. And if you bring this up again, I’ll find a new manager!<>

She hangs up on you, clearly unnerved by the conversation. You can’t blame her. But, you also don’t really like being threatened like that. Especially after you decisions have lead to her best performing video. But, you swallow it for now and get back to work. Hoping that she will understand in due time.

[img["ressources/scene/bria/intro/bria.webp"]] <>Hello, hello! It’s so nice to meet you <> Alfie mods one of my online communities so when he said you might be able to help me grow my channel I got super excited!<>

You share in her excitement. Telling her that you will do everything you can to help her channel grow. As you talk to her, you take a quick look at the types of videos that she makes. Noting that they mostly seem to be homesteading style videos where she tells viewers how to make crafts, grow food, and utilize materials in thrifty ways to reduce waste and increase self reliance. Looking it at though, she has a disappointingly low view count per video considering how solid her production value is. But some of her videos have an oddly high spike in views by comparison. You aren’t certain about what the connection is, but you focus on that. Telling her that you will find the connection with her highest rated videos, and show her how to replicate those things for a higher and more consistent view count.

<>Oh I thought of that too but I just can NOT figure out what it is about them. I must have watched them like twenty times each. If you can figure that out I would be totally grateful<>

You promise her that it will be priority one to help get her channel skyrocketing in views. But the second priority you have is making sure she has goals of her own. So you ask her what content plans she has already made for channel growth.

<>I have soooo many videos planned. Some have to wait a long time though. I have a series dedicated entirely to canning foods and showing people how fresh food can keep for years when canned properly<>

You go back and forth with Bria like this for a while. Figuring out a good few ideas for her channel as you discuss things. You don’t give away any of these ideas just yet, because she has yet to properly hire you. But you mostly wrap up the conversation explaining your fee to her and asking if she would like to work with you.

<>Absolutely! You are totally hired. I can not wait to work with you more! I’m so excited!<>

With that confirmation you say goodbye, and get ready to get to work. You’re Bria’s manager now. And you have to make her a star. Hopefully you can figure out the common thread of her more successful videos soon. Once you do, you’re sure that he channel will really pop.

Suddenly, your computer begins to notify you of an incoming video call. You answer the call and see Ana, looking absolutely disheveled. You greet her, but then instantly ask her if something is wrong. She looks like she is on the verge of tears.

[img["ressources/scene/anastasia/stage2/crying.webp"]] <>Get to my house. I need to talk to you in person<>

[[You arrive at Ana’s home|Anastasia Stage 2][$scene to 0]]<> <>

Now that you’re back at your desk, you pull out your phone and video call Anastasia. It barely rings before she answers. Clearly she was already on her phone when you called. When the video loads, it shows her all dolled up at some sort of resort. Based on how she is dressed, and her location, you presume you you caught her while she was working.

[img["ressources/scene/anastasia/intro/anastasia.webp"]] <>Yeah, hello? Hurry up I’m losing this fantastic lighting. What do you want?<>

You’re taken aback at how blunt and coarse she is. One sentence in and you already understand why she doesn’t already have someone managing her. You stay professional though, introducing yourself and explaining that your friend Alfie told you that she was in need of some help growing her Quikpik page.

<>Alfie? Oh that simp. Yeah he’s not wrong. I post fire pictures, like twelve every damn day. And I get so many fucking likes too. People comment like crazy, telling me how hot I am. I already know, but they say it anyway<>

You become a bit confused as you listen to her. By the way she explains it her page sounds like it’s incredibly popular. And as you pull it up and look, you can see that she’s telling the truth. She is constantly growing and gets insane amounts of engagement. You’re not even sure that there is much you could even do to help her grow at this point. So you ask her point blank that if her page does so well, why does she need help?

<>Because sponsors are dumb as hell. Girls that I am WAY hotter than get sponsored all the time but whenever I try to get one I get told to fuck off. They’re obviously idiots. I need someone to show them that for me<>

You can’t help but see why people don’t want to work with her. She’s probably cursed out every contact she’s had. But she isn’t wrong. She has the reach to make sponsors a lot of money. And in turn make her some decent cash as well. If you can get the right sponsors in front of her, you could skim a pretty penny off the top by working with her. So you tell her that you’ll take the job if she wants you.

<>Of course you will. You’d be dumb not to. Now get to it. I want sponsors kissing my boots<>

You chuckle at first, but when she doesn’t you can tell that she wasn’t joking. And in that moment you realize that it might be harder than your thought to help Anastasia out. But you still see the potential. You just have to cultivate it. You tell her to get back to the grind and that you’ll reach out to her soon. She hangs up without even saying goodbye. You’re going to have to make this bitch soften up a bit if you want to make some real cash through her. But for now, it’s time to get to work.

There were three major segments of the stream. Rose played a narrative decision based game, she played a shooter, and she played a dancing game. Looking at her viewer numbers, they clearly spiked the most during the segment with the dancing game. At first, you consider that it simply took that long for her audience to filter in, because it was the middle of the stream that this segment was a part of. But two other metrics changed your mind on this. The first is that she had a spike in first time chatters during this time. And the second is just how many viewers she lost after that segment was over. The conclusion you draw is simply that people like to see her dance. You call Rose to discuss these findings with her.

<>Hey <> What’s going on?<>

You greet her then go right into explaining your findings. Saying that her best content is her dancing segment.

<>Oh thank you so much! I have so much fun doing that game. And my chat always loves it too! They get so much more talkative<>

You specify that she seemed to get a lot of first time viewers during that segment. Really trying to emphasize the impact that it had. But she doesn’t quite seems to fully understand that you’re telling her the dancing brought in new viewers. She seems to just think that you personally want to see more of it.

<>You are so sweet! You don’t have to keep complimenting my dancing though! Not everyone likes it as much as you. I’ll send you some videos of me dancing personally since you like them so much! Talk to you soon!<>

She hangs up before you can stop her. You decide not to call her back. It’s plain to see that you’ll have to take a different approach if you want to try and get her to understand how her content affects her viewership. For now though, it is best to just keep monitoring for spikes in viewership. Perhaps you’ll see something new that will change your mind next time. In the meantime though, Rose does follow through and send you that video of her dancing. Luckily for you she didn’t seem to edit it before sending. As halfway through the dance, her tits popped out. Sipping on some boba tea while you speak with her.

[img["ressources/scene/rose/intro/rose.webp"]] <>Hi hi! $mc.name right? I’m so glad you could come by! I had a friend say that I need a manager. No clue why but it sounded like a smart idea. So do you want the job?<>

You smile, and say that you would love the job. But you ask if she even knows what it means to have a manager, or if there is anything specific that she wants you to do for her. She looks confused for a second before answering.

<>Oh! I hadn’t really thought about it. My stream goes really smooth already. What I really need is someone to remind me about the stuff I plan for stream, and someone who can help me like, expand my audience. Ya know what I mean?<>

You say you can do all of that for her and more. She doesn’t seem to know much about what a manager is supposed to do for her. So you explain it to her more directly. Saying that you’ll work to keep her on track and on schedule, help her get more sponsorships, and work with other managers to schedule some collaborations in the future.

<>That all sounds so freaking cool! So I can just focus on streaming while you do all of that for me? I’m down, where do I sign!<>

You laugh and tell her that you’ll get paper work over to her later. But for now you want to go over what she means by expanding her audience.

<>Yeah I have such a great and devoted audience. But it hasn’t really grown in a while. I want more people in my chat! But I don’t to really change my stream either. I want the people who already watch to still enjoy it, ya know?<>

You understand completely and lay out your plan for how you will try and fix this for her. Explaining that you’ll start by catching some of her streams and seeing when the viewership spikes the most. passages.name: Interact With Erika
passages.source_raw:
<><>

Earlier today you sent a few work orders over to Erika to be completed. And as the day goes on, one by one each one comes back in. With how quickly they were done you presume that she just made them bland and uninspired. But as you review them, you are pleasantly surprised to see that they are in fact spectacular in all respects. In one day she programmed three websites with stunning complexity and impeccable design. They are easy to use, intuitive, and beautiful. Finally, the results you were looking for when you hired her. She even sent an email to you asking you to send her more orders for the day. You decide that you’ll hand deliver them yourself, so that you can compliment her on her work while you do.

You walk into the open door of her office, closing it behind you and closing the blinds. With how some of your visits to Erika’s office have gone, it’s just smarter to be safe and do that the moment you walk in. You turn towards Erika and drop some files for some more work orders on her desk. She barely even notices you, snatching the files and getting right to work. It seems like you might have done too good of a job motivating her to work hard. She looks like a woman possessed. You walk around the desk and grab hold of her wrist to get her attention. She snaps out of her coding trance and looks up at you confused.

<>Hey, what’s up. I’m in a groove here<>

You tell her that she needs a break every now and then or she will burn herself out. You are surprised you need to teach her that. But, this might be the perfect time for the final lesson you can teach her. The value of a break and how it can empower your motivation. You tell her to stand up and you lead her over to the couch in her office. You sit beside her and lean back, enjoying the cushions. She is no stranger to relaxing, doing the same right after you.

<>I don’t get you. I thought you wanted me to be motivated and work hard on the websites<>

You tell her that that is exactly what you want. But you explain to her that you don’t want her to experience burnout. And that you think burnout might be part of why she lost so much motivation in the first place.

<>So what, I should just stop working when I’m on a roll and doing good work?<>

You say that she always will need a break during the day. And you hint further that you can think of some ways to distract her if she is struggling to relax. She smiles coyly, knowing exactly what you are implying.

passages.name: Intern pool
passages.source_raw:
<>

The Mayoral race is heating up as it gets closer and closer towards election day. You’re looking to get any extra boost or push that you can. As it gets later and later in the race, most people have already made up their mind on who they plan on voting for. It would take something rather significant to move the needle on even some of the less committed voters at this point. And you realize that it might be time to try and use the relationship you’ve built up with the intern, Mary Willis, to see if you can get something from her that could sway voters away from Cynthia.

You head to her cubicle and greet her as she fills out some paperwork. You see her work with blinding speed as usual. But pay very little attention to what she is actually working on. You ask her very directly, if she could do you a favor. The stern tone in your voice makes her set her flowery pen down and give you her full attention.

<>I’ll try my best! What do you need help with?<>

You say that you wanted to know if she had anything that could help you in the Mayoral race. Specifying that if she knew about anything that could lessen Cynthia’s public image, or something that could even raise your own, would be a great help. She cringes a bit at the request, clearly not comfortable with the question.

<>I don’t know <>. It doesn’t feel right to betray Ms. Wallace’s trust like that. She did hire me after all<>

You say you understand. You apologize for making such a big ask. Although, you slyly pull at her ambitions and heart strings to try and get her to change her mind. Saying that you made a promise to her that you would give her that staff position as Mayor. But you’re worried that without her help you might not win. She looks a little guilty while hearing you say this.

<>Well, you have helped me out so much. Heck the first day we met you helped me out with those papers I dropped on the floor. You were a real life saver Ms. Wallace would have fired my butt if weren’t for you. And then the time with the coffee, oh I don’t know<>

You tell her not to worry, trying to be as nice as possible as you start to walk away. Hoping that her kind nature takes over and pushes her to give in.

<>$mc.name…<>

Her soft voice tells you that it worked as you turn back around and look at her, waiting for her to say why she called you back.

<>Okay, I know one thing that will help. But please swear to me that you won’t say that you got this from me<>

You of course swear to that. As long as the information is good, then the source doesn’t matter. Mary pulls open one of her desk drawers and hands you a flash drive.

<>This is an email that I was sent by mistake. I forwarded it to Ms. Wallace as it said it was for her. But I saved a copy on this flash drive just in case. The email, I believe, is discussing a bribe that Ms. Wallace took as Mayor. Seriously you cannot let that get back to me<>

You promise her that you will do everything in your power to remove any hint of a trace that she knew anything about this email or how you obtained it. You thank her heavily, reaffirming your promise of the staff position once you’re the Mayor.

She looks concerned but trusting of you as you leave. Taking the flash drive back to your campaign headquarters and giving it to campaign.manager to subtly release to the media. Several groups are going to really hate this news and you are certain to get a pretty solid bump from this. Mary came through and your hard work getting close to her has more than paid off.

<> <> <> [[Continue|Campaign HQ][$mary.collusion to 1]]<> <>

With the election in the rear view mirror, you start to make good on the many promises and deals you made along the way. One such promise, was that you would give Mary a staff position once you became the Mayor. So you head to the intern pool and find Mary’s cubicle. She seems to be typing something up just as you arrive. You knock on the wall of her cubicle to let her know you’re there. Hearing the knock she turns around, he face forming a wide smile when she sees you.

<>$mc.name, Or should I say Mayor $mc.surname? Congratulations on winning the election!<>

You thank her for the congratulations, and playfully ask her what she is doing down here in the intern pool. She looks at you with a confused face.

<>I’m working? Are you doing okay? Did you celebrate your win too hard?<>

You chuckle, reminding her that you promised to make her a staffer once you won the election. She stands up, a little shocked. Almost as if she didn’t expect you to actually follow through with the promise. You explain that you find her to be a very positive person, and think that she would be the perfect choice to be your new press secretary. She looks like she is almost ready to cry with how happy and excited she is.

<>Ohmygod THANK YOU! I am so happy right now! I want to flip my desk! I won’t, because I can’t afford to replace the computer. BUT I REALLY WANT TO! Thank you Mayor $mc.surname! You have no idea how much this means to me<>

You tell her that she can call you by your name from now on. And add on that she is very welcome. She deserves the position and you make sure she knows that. You offer to show her her knew office. She grabs her personal items and follows you as you take her down the hall to what will soon be her official office. You explain that there is paperwork that needs to be filled out before it is completely official. But you can tell that the formality of that isn’t something that is on her mind as she explores the office around her.

<>This is amazing! I didn’t think you would even give me the job but, this? It’s a little overwhelming<>

You try and reassure her, saying that you know she is right for the job. You joke that if you knew you would win the election, then it stands to reason that you’ll be right about this one as well. She turns to you and smiles softly.

<>You’re right. I’m ready! I’m going to be scared out of my mind but this is the shot that I’ve been waiting for and I’m going to take it. No more second guessing myself. Now is the time for actions! So get those pants off now! It’s time for action!<>

Your eyes go wide for a moment. You certainly didn’t expect things to take a turn like this, but you certainly aren’t going to say no to the suggestion.

[[You take your pants off as instructed|Mary Stage 4][$scene to 0]] <>

You decide to give Mary a visit, heading to her cubicle and tapping on the wall of it to make your presence known. She turns around in her desk chair as smiles when she sees you. The smile is a little muted compared to usual though. She has a look of shame on her face that the smile is trying to hide.

<>Hey $mc.name how are you?<>

You tell her that you’re fine. But, you immediately turn the question back on her, noting that she seems to have something on her mind that is bothering her.

<>I’m fine as well. I would like to say something though. While I had a great time the other day, and I can’t thank you enough for helping make my day better after Ms. Wallace told me I couldn’t go to the press event, I feel ashamed about the whole thing<>

You feel a moment of worry, and apologize in advance in case she felt like you took advantage of her somewhat drunk state.

<>Oh goodness no! I was worried that I took advantage of you! I feel like I got drunk and embarrassed myself that night. That truly isn’t the type of person I try to be and I’m sorry I acted that way. Hell, I work for Ms. Wallace. I shouldn’t be fraternizing with her political rival. And I shouldn’t be betraying her by spending so much time with you either. Especially not when my future in this building could be in jeopardy<>

You grab Mary’s hand to calm her down as she starts to ramble. She smiles and blushes as you do. You tell her that your opinion of her wasn’t negatively affected by how she acted that night. Assuring her that it truly wasn’t a problem and that she has nothing to feel ashamed of. You continue, promising her something that Cynthia likely never would. You promise that as Mayor, you’ll give her a permanent staff position.

Noting that she is easily one of the fastest and most accomplished employees in this building. And that she is doing so as an intern. You think for a moment about how much she could help get done if she were a staffer instead and it makes you think that anything is possible.

<>You would make me a staffer? Just like that? I’m not sure I’ve earned that level of loyalty<>

You place your hand on her shoulder and say that it isn’t loyalty that is making you offer this to her. It’s her skills that has earned this. And you plan to make it right as the Mayor one day. The shame in her smile disappears as she beams with excitement.

<>I’m not sure I can even explain how much this means to me <>. Um… would you like to join me for dinner tonight? I’m not sure how else I can thank you and I am NOT letting this go without some kind of thank you. You are being too kind and I will repay that!<>

You chuckle, saying you’ll gladly come over. You head out to let her get back to work, saying you look forward to seeing her tonight. As you leave you think to yourself that you should grab a bottle of wine from the Strange Shop before heading over. Its never right to go to dinner empty handed.

[[Continue|City hall][$mary.questmain to 2.2]]<> <>

Mary’s desk is easy to spot in the pool of intern cubicles. Its the one with the largest stack of papers on it. Large enough that they peak over the walls of the cubicle for all to see. Although, you have to note that even if cluttered with mountains of paperwork, Mary’s desk is one of the cleanest that you’ve ever seen. It reminds you of the overachieving girl in middle school, the one who had color coded folders for every subject. Always used a pencil that had some sort of weirdly large eraser charm. And would shoot her hand up the moment the teacher asked a question. In fact, the pen on Mary’s desk right now is made out of a flower.

[img["ressources/scene/mary/stage1/pen.webp"]]

As you’re looking around her desk, Mary herself walks in and takes a seat.

<>Hey Mr. $mc.surname! Sorry I wasn’t here, I was getting coffee for Ms. Wallace. What can I do for you?<>

You begin to say that you just wanted to spend some time with her, get to know her better, and were wondering if she wanted to get coffee. If you want to get her help in taking down Cynthia, you need to get closer to her. Although, before you can finish, the phone on her desk rings. She puts a finger up stopping you.

<>I’m so sorry, but this is Ms. Wallace. I need to answer it<>

She picks up the phone and screams come through the receiver. Loud enough that you can almost make out what Cynthia is saying. She clearly is unhappy with the coffee that she was given. Something about the wrong type of creamer was used.

<>I’m so sorry Miss I promise you I asked for full cream not half and half. I’ll fix this right away<>

There is a bit more screaming coming through the phone before Cynthia finally hangs up. Mary sighs, looking at the mountain of paperwork she still has to do.

<>I have no clue how I’m going to get all of this done. I guess I’ll have to stay late again. I’m sorry Mr. $mc.surname, but I need to go. If Ms. Wallace doesn’t get her coffee soon she might actually throw a chair at me<>

You think that this will be the perfect opportunity to get in good with Mary, and stop her from leaving. Telling her that you’ll go back and get the coffee for her. Saying that she should just stay here and get the important work done.

<>Oh no no no, I can’t ask you to do that for me. It’s my job to take care of all of this. It’s part of why I’m here, to learn!<>

You tell her that she isn’t asking, you’re offering. And you note that she won’t learn anything by fixing coffee orders. You reiterate, asking her what the proper order is so that you can get it.

<>Well, if you’re certain. Ms. Wallace wants a dark roast iced coffee with double full cream and triple sugar. Are you really sure I can do it I pro-<>

You stop her before she can finish. Telling her to sit down and do the real work while you go get the coffee. She does as you say, looking unsure but finally getting to work on the veritable mountain of paperwork laid out in front of her.

[[Head out and grab the coffee|Mary Stage 1][$scene to 0]] <>

You spend some time talking with Mary at her desk in the intern pool. You talk with her a bit while she works. She is a very interesting woman. And the fact that she can work and hold a full conversation at the same time is rather impressive to you. Of course multitasking skills like this is probably exactly why she got this internship to begin with.

[img["ressources/scene/mary/locs/cityhall.webp"]] <>I think you would love my cats. One is named cow because he is white with black spots. And the other is cinnamon because he is red like cinnamon. They are both so sweet!<> <> [[Get going|City hall][$mary.gallery[7] to 1]]<> <>

There is nothing to do here right now.

[[Leave|City hall]] <>

When I was your age, my name was Jeff. I was a low level guy like you. Running drugs, making deliveries, doing whatever they asked me too. And I made good money. Even made enough to share it with others. People who made things that I liked. And then one day I sat in Don Leone’s office, just like you are now. And asked to take on more responsibility, just like you are, right, now. I’m proud of you <>. You’re following in my footsteps just like I thought you would. I got a job for you. Take Suzy, and hold up the bodega on third street. You do this, and impress me, we’ll have a conversation about having you do more for the family. Now get outta here<>

You thank him for the opportunity and head out to find Suzy. She is in her little shop like usual, wiping up the counters and keeping the place spotless. You tell her the good news, and explain what your Uncle wants her to help you with.

<>The bodega on third street? I coulda swore someone already hit that place this month. Lemme make a call real quick. I just wanna be sure. Meet me outback by my car. I’ll be out in a few<> [[Head to Suzy’s car|Mafia Promotion 1][$scene to 1]]<><> <>

You lean against the passenger side door of Suzy’s car, waiting until she heads out of the casino and meets up with you. She looks pleased as she approaches the car. You ask her if everything is good with the plan.

<>Yeah, we’re good now. Get in, let’s head to the bodega before word travels<>

You step into the car and before your seat belt clicks into place she is speeding off. As you start to get closer, you ask if she has a mask you can use. She looks at you in disbelief.

<>You empty inside or something? How’re ya gonna go on a job without a mask? Look in the back I think I got some new stockings you can use<>

You look back and she was right, a pair of beige pantyhose that she had just bought. You promise to pay to replace them as you slide them over your face to obscure your appearance. Suzy pulls into the ally behind the bodega and you both get out. There is a security guard there at the door. So Suzy pops out first.

<>I’ll distract him. Don’t waste no time<>

She hops out of the car and goes up to the guard. You can’t hear what they’re saying. But it becomes pretty clear how Suzy intends to distract the guard once she pulls her shirt up and shows off her tits.

The cashier is a little frantic, but manages to get the drawer open and starts stuffing the cash inside into a plastic bag.

Just as they finish filling the bag, you hear the whine of a police siren getting close. You look around, wondering who called the cops. But see everyone still on the floor. You snatch the bag out of the cashier’s hand and book it out back. But, once you’re outside, Suzy’s car is gone. You aren’t sure what to do so you just book it towards the Red Light District, hoping to avoid being seen by the police arriving at the scene.

You have to hop three fences before you finally feel like you are far enough away from the bodega, and the police, to pull off your mask. You stuff the bag of money into your coat to hide it as you start walking slowly and nonchalantly the rest of the way back to the casino. Just then, a car pulls up beside you and Suzy yells at you.

<>Get in ya dumbass!<>

You hop into her car, giving her a scowl as she drives off. You ask her where the hell she went. She looks around skittishly as she is driving. Clearly trying to avoid police at all costs.

Walking through the mall you notice Mary sitting on a bench by the fountain. She is eating a slice of pizza from the food court and looks like she’s just been given bad news. You head over to her to see what’s wrong. Calling out her name as you get close. When she sees you, she perks up a bit, calling back to you happily with a bit of pizza still in her mouth.

<>Mr. $mc.surname! Hello!<>

She swallows the pizza to speak more clearly as you get closer. You take a seat beside her on the bench and ask her why she looked so sad a moment ago. She points to a couple bags between her legs as she answers.

<>Ms. Wallace is having a press event tonight and she asked me to pick up a few things for her. I thought I was invited as well, so I got myself a nice dress. Only to find out a few minutes ago that I’m not actually invited after all. I could have sworn Ms. Wallace told me to dress nicely. But I guess I must have misunderstood<>

She keeps a smile on her face but her eyes betray how she really feels in the moment. You decide to try and cheer her up. You suggest that if she can’t go to this event, then the two of you can make an event of your own for the rest of the day. She looks at you with an incredulous smile.

<>What do you mean? Like rent out a venue for just us two to hang out?<>

You say that a venue isn’t needed. Noting that you’re already at the mall. The mall has everything you need to be able to have fun. From an arcade, to shops, to food, and even drinks. You grab her hand and offer to lead her on a bit of an adventure. She pops up from the bench, smiling wider than you’ve seen her smile before.

<>Let’s do it! This sounds like fun! I’ll race ya to the arcade!<>

You follow Mary up the stairs to the arcade. She does a cute little dance to celebrate getting there first. Then you both spend a while playing games. She wins some but you win more. Going through until you’ve played almost every game that the two of you have any interest in playing together.

<<widget "QuestMarkers">>
<<switch _args[0]>>

	<<if $halloween2021.active && $eris.questmain is 0>>

	<<else>>

	<</if>>

	<<else>>

	<<if $mikaela.questmain is 3 && $mikaela.int gte 20 && $startup.workScore gt $mikaela.workScore>>

	<<else>>

	<</if>>

	<<if $grandma.questmain is 2 && $grandma.int gte 5>>

	<<else>>
		<<set _grandmamark to 0>>
	<</if>>
<<case "Park">>
	<<if $cousin.questmain is 2 && $cousin.trust gte 15 && $cousin.corr gte 10>>

	<<else>>
		<<set _cousinmark to 0>>
	<</if>>
	<<if $dean.questmain is 3 && $dean.route is "dom" && $dean.trust gte 15 && $mc.dom gte 20>>
		<<set _deanmark to 1>>
	<<else>>
		<<set _deanmark to 0>>

	<<else>>
		<<set _jennamark to 0>>
	<</if>>

	<<else>>

	<<else>>

	<<else>>

	<</if>>
	<<if $hana.questmain is 2 && $hana.trust gte 25>>

	<<else>>

	<<else>>
		<<set _amandamark to 0>>
	<</if>>
<<case "Interact With Employees">>
	<<if $mom.questmain gte 9 && $mom.trust gte 25 && $mom.corr gte 10 && $tammy.questmain is 4>>
		<<set _mommark to 1>>
	<<else>>
		<<set _mommark to 0>>
	<</if>>
	<<if ($tammy.questmain is 3 && $tammy.trust gte 20 && $startup.level gte 3) || ($tammy.questmain is 1 && $tammy.trust gte 10)>>
		<<set _tammymark to 1>>
	<<else>>
		<<set _tammymark to 0>>
	<</if>>
	<<if ($erika.questmain is 3 && $erika.trust gte 20 && $erika.dev gte 3) || ($erika.questmain is 2 && $erika.trust gte 15 && $erika.dev gte 2) || ($erika.questmain is 0 && $erika.trust gte 5) || ($erika.mot gte 100 && $erika.dev lt 3)>>

	<<else>>
